import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Dixmier conjecture

The Dixmier conjecture: any endomorphism of the Weyl algebras $A_1$ and $A_2$ is an automorphism.

Here $k$ is a field of characteristic zero and the $n$-th Weyl algebra $A_n$ is the unital
associative $k$-algebra with generators $x_1, \dots, x_n, \partial_1, \dots, \partial_n$ and
relations
$$[x_i, x_j] = 0, \quad [\partial_i, \partial_j] = 0, \quad [\partial_i, x_j] = \delta_{ij}.$$
An endomorphism is a unital $k$-algebra homomorphism $A_n \to A_n$, and it is an automorphism
when it is bijective.

The case $n = 1$ is the problem posed by Dixmier in 1968. The case $n = 2$ is a case of the
generalized Dixmier conjecture $DC_n$. By Tsuchimoto and Belov-Kanel–Kontsevich, $DC_n$ implies
the Jacobian conjecture $JC_n$ in $n$ variables, and $JC_{2n}$ implies $DC_n$. The Jacobian
conjecture is false in three variables, so $DC_n$ is false for all $n \geq 3$, and the conjecture
is only stated for $A_1$ and $A_2$.

The Weyl algebra is not in Mathlib, so this file defines it as the quotient of the free algebra
on the generators $x_i$, $\partial_i$ by the relations above.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, *List of unsolved problems in mathematics*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Wikipedia, *Dixmier conjecture*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dixmier_conjecture)
- [J. Dixmier, *Sur les algèbres de Weyl*, Bull. Soc. Math. France 96 (1968), 209–242](http://www.numdam.org/item?id=BSMF_1968__96__209_0)
- [A. Belov-Kanel, M. Kontsevich, *The Jacobian conjecture is stably equivalent to the Dixmier conjecture*](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0512171)
- [A. Zheglov, *The Conjecture of Dixmier for the first Weyl algebra is true*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.06959)
-/
namespace DixmierConjecture
section WeylAlgebra
variable (k : Type*) [CommRing k] (σ : Type*)
namespace WeylAlgebra

blocks.code:
inductive Rel : FreeAlgebra k (σ ⊕ σ) → FreeAlgebra k (σ ⊕ σ) → Prop
  /-- The coordinates commute: $x_i x_j = x_j x_i$. -/
  | x_mul_x (i j : σ) : Rel (ι k (.inl i) * ι k (.inl j)) (ι k (.inl j) * ι k (.inl i))
  /-- The partial derivatives commute: $\partial_i \partial_j = \partial_j \partial_i$. -/
  | d_mul_d (i j : σ) : Rel (ι k (.inr i) * ι k (.inr j)) (ι k (.inr j) * ι k (.inr i))
  /-- The canonical commutation relation: $\partial_i x_i = x_i \partial_i + 1$. -/
  | d_mul_x_self (i : σ) : Rel (ι k (.inr i) * ι k (.inl i)) (ι k (.inl i) * ι k (.inr i) + 1)
  /-- Distinct indices commute: $\partial_i x_j = x_j \partial_i$ for $i \ne j$. -/
  | d_mul_x_of_ne {i j : σ} (h : i ≠ j) :
    Rel (ι k (.inr i) * ι k (.inl j)) (ι k (.inl j) * ι k (.inr i))

justification.closest_existing_considered: Mathlib has no Weyl algebra (grepped `Weyl` in Mathlib and the repo: only Weyl groups of root systems). `TensorAlgebra.Rel` / `CliffordAlgebra.Rel` are the analogous constructions but define different algebras.

justification.why_needed: The defining relations of the Weyl algebra on `FreeAlgebra k (σ ⊕ σ)` (coordinates commute, derivatives commute, ∂_i x_i = x_i ∂_i + 1, ∂_i x_j = x_j ∂_i for i ≠ j); needed to present the Weyl algebra as a quotient, exactly as Mathlib presents `TensorAlgebra`/`CliffordAlgebra` via `RingQuot`.

blocks.name: Rel
blocks.text:
open FreeAlgebra in
/-- The defining relations of the Weyl algebra, as a relation on the free algebra with generators
`Sum.inl i` (the coordinate $x_i$) and `Sum.inr i` (the partial derivative $\partial_i$). -/
inductive Rel : FreeAlgebra k (σ ⊕ σ) → FreeAlgebra k (σ ⊕ σ) → Prop
  /-- The coordinates commute: $x_i x_j = x_j x_i$. -/
  | x_mul_x (i j : σ) : Rel (ι k (.inl i) * ι k (.inl j)) (ι k (.inl j) * ι k (.inl i))
  /-- The partial derivatives commute: $\partial_i \partial_j = \partial_j \partial_i$. -/
  | d_mul_d (i j : σ) : Rel (ι k (.inr i) * ι k (.inr j)) (ι k (.inr j) * ι k (.inr i))
  /-- The canonical commutation relation: $\partial_i x_i = x_i \partial_i + 1$. -/
  | d_mul_x_self (i : σ) : Rel (ι k (.inr i) * ι k (.inl i)) (ι k (.inl i) * ι k (.inr i) + 1)
  /-- Distinct indices commute: $\partial_i x_j = x_j \partial_i$ for $i \ne j$. -/
  | d_mul_x_of_ne {i j : σ} (h : i ≠ j) :
    Rel (ι k (.inr i) * ι k (.inl j)) (ι k (.inl j) * ι k (.inr i))
end WeylAlgebra

blocks.docstring:
The Weyl algebra over `k` with coordinates and partial derivatives indexed by `σ`: the unital
associative `k`-algebra generated by $x_i$, $\partial_i$ ($i \in \sigma$) subject to
$[x_i, x_j] = 0$, $[\partial_i, \partial_j] = 0$ and $[\partial_i, x_j] = \delta_{ij}$.
The $n$-th Weyl algebra $A_n$ is `WeylAlgebra k (Fin n)`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Considered instead the subalgebra of `Module.End k (MvPolynomial (Fin n) k)` generated by multiplication by `X i` and `pderiv i` (differential operators). This coincides with A_n only in characteristic zero and is less transparently 'the Weyl algebra'; the generators-and-relations presentation is the textbook/BK definition, and the file also provides the map to differential operators (`toDiffOp`) as a sanity check.
justification.name: DixmierConjecture.WeylAlgebra
justification.why_needed: The Weyl algebra `A_σ := RingQuot (WeylAlgebra.Rel k σ)` with `Ring` and `Algebra k` instances; the n-th Weyl algebra A_n is `WeylAlgebra k (Fin n)`. The Weyl algebra is absent from Mathlib and FormalConjecturesForMathlib.

/-- The Weyl algebra over `k` with coordinates and partial derivatives indexed by `σ`: the unital

def WeylAlgebra := RingQuot (WeylAlgebra.Rel k σ)

@[category API, AMS 16]
lemma d_mul_x_sub_x_mul_d_eq_ite [DecidableEq σ] (i j : σ) :
    d k i * x k j - x k j * d k i = if i = j then 1 else 0 := by
  split_ifs with h
  · subst h
    exact d_mul_x_sub_x_mul_d k i
  · rw [d_mul_x_of_ne k h, sub_self]
blocks.name: d_mul_x_sub_x_mul_d_eq_ite
blocks.text:
/-- The commutation relation $[\partial_i, x_j] = \delta_{ij}$. -/
@[category API, AMS 16]
lemma d_mul_x_sub_x_mul_d_eq_ite [DecidableEq σ] (i j : σ) :
    d k i * x k j - x k j * d k i = if i = j then 1 else 0 := by
  split_ifs with h
  · subst h
    exact d_mul_x_sub_x_mul_d k i
  · rw [d_mul_x_of_ne k h, sub_self]

blocks.code:
noncomputable def toDiffOp : WeylAlgebra k σ →ₐ[k] Module.End k (MvPolynomial σ k) :=
  RingQuot.liftAlgHom k ⟨FreeAlgebra.lift k <| Sum.elim
      (fun i ↦ LinearMap.mulLeft k (MvPolynomial.X i))
      (fun i ↦ (MvPolynomial.pderiv i).toLinearMap), by
    intro a b h
    induction h with
    | x_mul_x i j =>
      refine LinearMap.ext fun p ↦ ?_
      simp [mul_left_comm]
    | d_mul_d i j =>
      refine LinearMap.ext fun p ↦ ?_
      have : ⁅MvPolynomial.pderiv (R := k) i, MvPolynomial.pderiv j⁆ = 0 :=
        MvPolynomial.derivation_ext fun l ↦ by
          rw [Derivation.commutator_apply]
          obtain rfl | hli := eq_or_ne l i <;> obtain rfl | hlj := eq_or_ne l j <;> simp [*]
      simpa [Derivation.commutator_apply, sub_eq_zero] using DFunLike.congr_fun this p
    | d_mul_x_self i =>
      refine LinearMap.ext fun p ↦ ?_
      simp [add_comm]
    | d_mul_x_of_ne h =>
      refine LinearMap.ext fun p ↦ ?_
      simp [MvPolynomial.pderiv_X_of_ne h.symm]⟩
blocks.docstring:
The standard representation of the Weyl algebra by differential operators with polynomial
coefficients: $x_i$ acts on `MvPolynomial σ k` as multiplication by `X i`, and $\partial_i$ acts
as `pderiv i`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: No existing map from a presented Weyl algebra to differential operators exists in Mathlib; built with `RingQuot.liftAlgHom` and `FreeAlgebra.lift`.
justification.name: DixmierConjecture.WeylAlgebra.toDiffOp
justification.why_needed: The standard representation of the Weyl algebra on `MvPolynomial σ k` (x_i ↦ `LinearMap.mulLeft k (X i)`, ∂_i ↦ `pderiv i`), used to prove `Nontrivial (WeylAlgebra k σ)` so that the conjecture is not degenerate. API only; not used in the conjecture statements.

blocks.name: toDiffOp
blocks.text:
variable (σ) in
/-- The standard representation of the Weyl algebra by differential operators with polynomial
coefficients: $x_i$ acts on `MvPolynomial σ k` as multiplication by `X i`, and $\partial_i$ acts
as `pderiv i`. -/
noncomputable def toDiffOp : WeylAlgebra k σ →ₐ[k] Module.End k (MvPolynomial σ k) :=
  RingQuot.liftAlgHom k ⟨FreeAlgebra.lift k <| Sum.elim
      (fun i ↦ LinearMap.mulLeft k (MvPolynomial.X i))
      (fun i ↦ (MvPolynomial.pderiv i).toLinearMap), by
    intro a b h
    induction h with
    | x_mul_x i j =>
      refine LinearMap.ext fun p ↦ ?_
      simp [mul_left_comm]
    | d_mul_d i j =>
      refine LinearMap.ext fun p ↦ ?_
      have : ⁅MvPolynomial.pderiv (R := k) i, MvPolynomial.pderiv j⁆ = 0 :=
        MvPolynomial.derivation_ext fun l ↦ by
          rw [Derivation.commutator_apply]
          obtain rfl | hli := eq_or_ne l i <;> obtain rfl | hlj := eq_or_ne l j <;> simp [*]
      simpa [Derivation.commutator_apply, sub_eq_zero] using DFunLike.congr_fun this p
    | d_mul_x_self i =>
      refine LinearMap.ext fun p ↦ ?_
      simp [add_comm]
    | d_mul_x_of_ne h =>
      refine LinearMap.ext fun p ↦ ?_
      simp [MvPolynomial.pderiv_X_of_ne h.symm]⟩

instance [Nontrivial k] : Nontrivial (WeylAlgebra k σ) :=

The Weyl algebra over a nontrivial ring is nontrivial, so the relations do not collapse
and the Dixmier conjecture is not trivially true.

lemma d_mul_x_ne_x_mul_d [Nontrivial k] (i : σ) : d k i * x k i ≠ x k i * d k i := by

@[category research open, AMS 14 16]
theorem dixmier_conjecture.parts.i (f : WeylAlgebra k (Fin 1) →ₐ[k] WeylAlgebra k (Fin 1)) :
    Function.Bijective f := by
  sorry
blocks.docstring:
The **Dixmier conjecture** for the first Weyl algebra $A_1$ (Dixmier's original 1968 problem,
$DC_1$): for any field $k$ of characteristic zero, every unital $k$-algebra endomorphism of
$A_1 = k\langle x, \partial \rangle / ([\partial, x] = 1)$ is an automorphism, i.e. is bijective.

A proof was announced by Zheglov in 2024, but the problem is still regarded as open.

$JC_4$ implies $DC_2$.

claims.decomposer_note: The A_1 case (Dixmier's original 1968 problem, DC_1): over any field k of characteristic zero (WLOG k = ℂ), every unital k-algebra endomorphism of the first Weyl algebra A_1 = k⟨x, ∂⟩/([∂, x] = 1) is an automorphism (i.e. bijective); the char-0 hypothesis and unitality are implicit in the list entry (Zheglov's 'non-zero endomorphism' phrasing is equivalent to unital), the Weyl algebra is not in Mathlib and must be defined, and the case is still classed open despite Zheglov's 2024 proposed proof.
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates state the same faithful proposition (arbitrary field k with CharZero, unital k-algebra endomorphism as AlgHom, automorphism as Function.Bijective, A_1 presented as the quotient of the free algebra on x, ∂ by [∂,x]=1), matching Dixmier/Belov-Kanel–Kontsevich/Zheglov. c02's Weyl-algebra definition was chosen as the base: generic index type σ, RingQuot by an inductive relation with no DecidableEq dependence, API lemmas verifying the relations in the quotient, the differential-operator representation and a proven Nontrivial instance (so the statement is not trivially true), all with no auxiliary MvPolynomial lemma. Edits: stated the slot directly as `(f : WeylAlgebra k (Fin 1) →ₐ[k] WeylAlgebra k (Fin 1)) : Function.Bijective f` (c08 style) instead of via the `DixmierConjectureProp` indirection; added a δ_ij commutator API lemma; dropped c02's extra non-slot theorems.
claims.source_text: any endomorphism of the Weyl algebras $A_{1}$ and $A_{2}$ is an automorphism
claims.text_span: any endomorphism of the Weyl algebras $A_{1}$ and $A_{2}$ is an automorphism

claims.decomposer_note: The A_2 case (generalized Dixmier conjecture DC_2): over any field k of characteristic zero, every unital k-algebra endomorphism of the second Weyl algebra A_2 (generators x_1, x_2, ∂_1, ∂_2 with [∂_i, x_j] = δ_ij and all other commutators zero) is an automorphism; this is a distinct question from DC_1 (DC_2 ⇒ DC_1 is known via Belov-Kanel–Kontsevich but not the converse), it is open because it is implied by the open JC_4 and implies the open JC_2, and the statement deliberately excludes A_n for n ≥ 3 where the conjecture is now known to be false.

Stated directly rather than through `DixmierConjectureProp`; only n = 1 and n = 2 are asserted, no A_n for n ≥ 3.

context:
In algebra, the Dixmier conjecture, stated by Jacques Dixmier in 1968, originally asked whether any endomorphism of the first Weyl algebra $A_{1}$ over a field of characteristic zero is an automorphism. The analogous statement for the $n$ -th Weyl algebra $A_{n}$ was recorded in 1982 by Bass, Connell, and Wright, who attributed it to communications from Leonid Vaserstein and Victor Kac, and was later referred to as the "generalized Dixmier conjecture".
Tsuchimoto in 2005, and independently Belov-Kanel and Kontsevich in 2007, showed that the Dixmier conjecture is stably equivalent to the Jacobian conjecture: the Dixmier conjecture for the n-th Weyl algebra $A_{n}$ implies the Jacobian conjecture for polynomial maps in n variables, while conversely the Jacobian conjecture in $2n$ variables implies the Dixmier conjecture for $A_{n}$. In July 2026, a counterexample to the Jacobian conjecture in three variables was found, which by the first of these implications shows that the Dixmier conjecture is false for $A_{n}$ for all $n\geq 3$.
The conjecture remains open for the first and second Weyl algebras, since the Jacobian conjecture is still open in two variables. The case of the first Weyl algebra $A_{1}$ was the problem originally posed by Dixmier; a proposed proof of this case was announced by Alexander Zheglov in 2024.

decomposition_objections.text: None. The split into the A_1 case (DC_1) and the A_2 case (DC_2) is correct: they are distinct open problems (DC_2 ⇒ DC_1 is known, the converse is not), and the list entry deliberately restricts to n = 1, 2 since DC_n is false for n ≥ 3. The notes' implicit hypotheses (char-0 field, unital k-algebra endomorphisms) agree with all primary sources and were adopted.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Dixmier conjecture

The Dixmier conjecture: any endomorphism of the Weyl algebras $A_1$ and $A_2$ is an automorphism.

Here $k$ is a field of characteristic zero and the $n$-th Weyl algebra $A_n$ is the unital
associative $k$-algebra with generators $x_1, \dots, x_n, \partial_1, \dots, \partial_n$ and
relations
$$[x_i, x_j] = 0, \quad [\partial_i, \partial_j] = 0, \quad [\partial_i, x_j] = \delta_{ij}.$$
An endomorphism is a unital $k$-algebra homomorphism $A_n \to A_n$, and it is an automorphism
when it is bijective.

The case $n = 1$ is the problem posed by Dixmier in 1968. The case $n = 2$ is a case of the
generalized Dixmier conjecture $DC_n$. By Tsuchimoto and Belov-Kanel–Kontsevich, $DC_n$ implies
the Jacobian conjecture $JC_n$ in $n$ variables, and $JC_{2n}$ implies $DC_n$. The Jacobian
conjecture is false in three variables, so $DC_n$ is false for all $n \geq 3$, and the conjecture
is only stated for $A_1$ and $A_2$.

The Weyl algebra is not in Mathlib, so this file defines it as the quotient of the free algebra
on the generators $x_i$, $\partial_i$ by the relations above.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, *List of unsolved problems in mathematics*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Wikipedia, *Dixmier conjecture*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dixmier_conjecture)
- [J. Dixmier, *Sur les algèbres de Weyl*, Bull. Soc. Math. France 96 (1968), 209–242](http://www.numdam.org/item?id=BSMF_1968__96__209_0)
- [A. Belov-Kanel, M. Kontsevich, *The Jacobian conjecture is stably equivalent to the Dixmier conjecture*](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0512171)
- [A. Zheglov, *The Conjecture of Dixmier for the first Weyl algebra is true*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.06959)
-/

namespace DixmierConjecture

section WeylAlgebra

variable (k : Type*) [CommRing k] (σ : Type*)

namespace WeylAlgebra

open FreeAlgebra in
/-- The defining relations of the Weyl algebra, as a relation on the free algebra with generators
`Sum.inl i` (the coordinate $x_i$) and `Sum.inr i` (the partial derivative $\partial_i$). -/
inductive Rel : FreeAlgebra k (σ ⊕ σ) → FreeAlgebra k (σ ⊕ σ) → Prop
  /-- The coordinates commute: $x_i x_j = x_j x_i$. -/
  | x_mul_x (i j : σ) : Rel (ι k (.inl i) * ι k (.inl j)) (ι k (.inl j) * ι k (.inl i))
  /-- The partial derivatives commute: $\partial_i \partial_j = \partial_j \partial_i$. -/
  | d_mul_d (i j : σ) : Rel (ι k (.inr i) * ι k (.inr j)) (ι k (.inr j) * ι k (.inr i))
  /-- The canonical commutation relation: $\partial_i x_i = x_i \partial_i + 1$. -/
  | d_mul_x_self (i : σ) : Rel (ι k (.inr i) * ι k (.inl i)) (ι k (.inl i) * ι k (.inr i) + 1)
  /-- Distinct indices commute: $\partial_i x_j = x_j \partial_i$ for $i \ne j$. -/
  | d_mul_x_of_ne {i j : σ} (h : i ≠ j) :
    Rel (ι k (.inr i) * ι k (.inl j)) (ι k (.inl j) * ι k (.inr i))

end WeylAlgebra

/-- The Weyl algebra over `k` with coordinates and partial derivatives indexed by `σ`: the unital
associative `k`-algebra generated by $x_i$, $\partial_i$ ($i \in \sigma$) subject to
$[x_i, x_j] = 0$, $[\partial_i, \partial_j] = 0$ and $[\partial_i, x_j] = \delta_{ij}$.
The $n$-th Weyl algebra $A_n$ is `WeylAlgebra k (Fin n)`. -/
def WeylAlgebra := RingQuot (WeylAlgebra.Rel k σ)

namespace WeylAlgebra

instance : Ring (WeylAlgebra k σ) := RingQuot.instRing _

instance : Algebra k (WeylAlgebra k σ) := RingQuot.instAlgebra _

variable {σ}

/-- The coordinate $x_i$ in the Weyl algebra. -/
def x (i : σ) : WeylAlgebra k σ := RingQuot.mkAlgHom k (Rel k σ) (FreeAlgebra.ι k (.inl i))

/-- The partial derivative $\partial_i$ in the Weyl algebra. -/
def d (i : σ) : WeylAlgebra k σ := RingQuot.mkAlgHom k (Rel k σ) (FreeAlgebra.ι k (.inr i))

@[category API, AMS 16]
lemma x_mul_x (i j : σ) : x k i * x k j = x k j * x k i := by
  simpa [x] using RingQuot.mkAlgHom_rel k (Rel.x_mul_x (k := k) i j)

@[category API, AMS 16]
lemma d_mul_d (i j : σ) : d k i * d k j = d k j * d k i := by
  simpa [d] using RingQuot.mkAlgHom_rel k (Rel.d_mul_d (k := k) i j)

@[category API, AMS 16]
lemma d_mul_x_self (i : σ) : d k i * x k i = x k i * d k i + 1 := by
  simpa [x, d] using RingQuot.mkAlgHom_rel k (Rel.d_mul_x_self (k := k) i)

@[category API, AMS 16]
lemma d_mul_x_of_ne {i j : σ} (h : i ≠ j) : d k i * x k j = x k j * d k i := by
  simpa [x, d] using RingQuot.mkAlgHom_rel k (Rel.d_mul_x_of_ne (k := k) h)

/-- The canonical commutation relation $[\partial_i, x_i] = 1$. -/
@[category API, AMS 16]
lemma d_mul_x_sub_x_mul_d (i : σ) : d k i * x k i - x k i * d k i = 1 := by
  rw [d_mul_x_self, add_sub_cancel_left]

/-- The commutation relation $[\partial_i, x_j] = \delta_{ij}$. -/
@[category API, AMS 16]
lemma d_mul_x_sub_x_mul_d_eq_ite [DecidableEq σ] (i j : σ) :
    d k i * x k j - x k j * d k i = if i = j then 1 else 0 := by
  split_ifs with h
  · subst h
    exact d_mul_x_sub_x_mul_d k i
  · rw [d_mul_x_of_ne k h, sub_self]

variable (σ) in
/-- The standard representation of the Weyl algebra by differential operators with polynomial
coefficients: $x_i$ acts on `MvPolynomial σ k` as multiplication by `X i`, and $\partial_i$ acts
as `pderiv i`. -/
noncomputable def toDiffOp : WeylAlgebra k σ →ₐ[k] Module.End k (MvPolynomial σ k) :=
  RingQuot.liftAlgHom k ⟨FreeAlgebra.lift k <| Sum.elim
      (fun i ↦ LinearMap.mulLeft k (MvPolynomial.X i))
      (fun i ↦ (MvPolynomial.pderiv i).toLinearMap), by
    intro a b h
    induction h with
    | x_mul_x i j =>
      refine LinearMap.ext fun p ↦ ?_
      simp [mul_left_comm]
    | d_mul_d i j =>
      refine LinearMap.ext fun p ↦ ?_
      have : ⁅MvPolynomial.pderiv (R := k) i, MvPolynomial.pderiv j⁆ = 0 :=
        MvPolynomial.derivation_ext fun l ↦ by
          rw [Derivation.commutator_apply]
          obtain rfl | hli := eq_or_ne l i <;> obtain rfl | hlj := eq_or_ne l j <;> simp [*]
      simpa [Derivation.commutator_apply, sub_eq_zero] using DFunLike.congr_fun this p
    | d_mul_x_self i =>
      refine LinearMap.ext fun p ↦ ?_
      simp [add_comm]
    | d_mul_x_of_ne h =>
      refine LinearMap.ext fun p ↦ ?_
      simp [MvPolynomial.pderiv_X_of_ne h.symm]⟩

@[category API, AMS 16]
lemma toDiffOp_x (i : σ) : toDiffOp k σ (x k i) = LinearMap.mulLeft k (MvPolynomial.X i) :=
  (RingQuot.liftAlgHom_mkAlgHom_apply _ _ _ _).trans (FreeAlgebra.lift_ι_apply _ _)

@[category API, AMS 16]
lemma toDiffOp_d (i : σ) : toDiffOp k σ (d k i) = (MvPolynomial.pderiv i).toLinearMap :=
  (RingQuot.liftAlgHom_mkAlgHom_apply _ _ _ _).trans (FreeAlgebra.lift_ι_apply _ _)

/-- The Weyl algebra over a nontrivial ring is nontrivial, so the relations do not collapse
and the Dixmier conjecture is not trivially true. -/
@[category API, AMS 16]
instance [Nontrivial k] : Nontrivial (WeylAlgebra k σ) :=
  (toDiffOp k σ).toRingHom.domain_nontrivial

/-- In a Weyl algebra over a nontrivial ring, $\partial_i$ and $x_i$ do not commute. -/
@[category test, AMS 16]
lemma d_mul_x_ne_x_mul_d [Nontrivial k] (i : σ) : d k i * x k i ≠ x k i * d k i := by
  rw [Ne, ← sub_eq_zero, d_mul_x_sub_x_mul_d]
  exact one_ne_zero

end WeylAlgebra

end WeylAlgebra

section Conjecture

variable {k : Type*} [Field k] [CharZero k]

/-- The **Dixmier conjecture** for the first Weyl algebra $A_1$ (Dixmier's original 1968 problem,
$DC_1$): for any field $k$ of characteristic zero, every unital $k$-algebra endomorphism of
$A_1 = k\langle x, \partial \rangle / ([\partial, x] = 1)$ is an automorphism, i.e. is bijective.

A proof was announced by Zheglov in 2024, but the problem is still regarded as open. -/
@[category research open, AMS 14 16]
theorem dixmier_conjecture.parts.i (f : WeylAlgebra k (Fin 1) →ₐ[k] WeylAlgebra k (Fin 1)) :
    Function.Bijective f := by
  sorry

/-- The **Dixmier conjecture** for the second Weyl algebra $A_2$ (the generalized Dixmier conjecture
$DC_2$): for any field $k$ of characteristic zero, every unital $k$-algebra endomorphism of
$A_2$, the $k$-algebra with generators $x_1, x_2, \partial_1, \partial_2$ and relations
$[\partial_i, x_j] = \delta_{ij}$, $[x_i, x_j] = 0$, $[\partial_i, \partial_j] = 0$,
is an automorphism, i.e. is bijective.

By Tsuchimoto and Belov-Kanel–Kontsevich, $DC_2$ implies the Jacobian conjecture $JC_2$, and
$JC_4$ implies $DC_2$. -/
@[category research open, AMS 14 16]
theorem dixmier_conjecture.parts.ii (f : WeylAlgebra k (Fin 2) →ₐ[k] WeylAlgebra k (Fin 2)) :
    Function.Bijective f := by
  sorry

end Conjecture

end DixmierConjecture

items: Field hypothesis: the list entry does not mention the base field; following the Wikipedia article, Dixmier (1968), Belov-Kanel–Kontsevich and Zheglov, both slots are stated for an arbitrary field `k` with `[Field k] [CharZero k]` (universe-polymorphic `k : Type*`). The literature notes it is WLOG k = ℂ, but the general char-0 formulation is the standard one and is what is stated.

'Endomorphism' is read as a unital k-algebra homomorphism `A →ₐ[k] A` (Mathlib `AlgHom`s are unital). This matches BK's 'endomorphism of the n-th Weyl algebra A_{n,k} over k' and Zheglov's `End_K(A_1)`; Zheglov's 'non-zero endomorphism' phrasing is equivalent since A_1 is a domain. Non-k-linear ring endomorphisms are NOT included, consistent with the literature.
'Is an automorphism' is rendered as `Function.Bijective f`; a bijective `AlgHom` is exactly an `AlgEquiv` (`AlgEquiv.ofBijective`), so this is equivalent to `f` being a k-algebra automorphism.

Weyl algebra definition: `WeylAlgebra k σ := RingQuot (WeylAlgebra.Rel k σ)` where `Rel` is an inductive relation on `FreeAlgebra k (σ ⊕ σ)` with generators `Sum.inl i` = x_i, `Sum.inr i` = ∂_i and relations x_i x_j = x_j x_i, ∂_i ∂_j = ∂_j ∂_i, ∂_i x_i = x_i ∂_i + 1, and ∂_i x_j = x_j ∂_i for i ≠ j. This is the presentation of A_n by generators and relations with [∂_i, x_j] = δ_ij exactly as in the decomposition notes and in BK (with y_i = x_i, y_{n+i} = ∂_i). A_n is `WeylAlgebra k (Fin n)`. The sign convention [∂, x] = 1 is the one used by the notes and by Zheglov (Dixmier's [p,q] = 1 is the same algebra with p = ∂, q = x).

Non-degeneracy check: the file constructs the standard representation `toDiffOp : WeylAlgebra k σ →ₐ[k] Module.End k (MvPolynomial σ k)` (x_i ↦ multiplication by X i, ∂_i ↦ pderiv i) and derives `Nontrivial (WeylAlgebra k σ)` for nontrivial k, plus a test that ∂_i and x_i do not commute, so the conjecture is not vacuous/degenerate.

Extra (non-slot) declarations included alongside the two slots, following the Oppermann-file precedent: `dixmier_conjecture` (the conjunction of both parts, i.e. the list entry verbatim, `research open`), and `dixmier_conjecture.variants.not_of_three_le` (`¬ DixmierConjectureProp k n` for n ≥ 3 over any char-0 field, `research solved`), the latter recorded because the article states DC_n is false for n ≥ 3 via DC_n ⇒ JC_n and the 3-variable Jacobian counterexample that the repo's JacobianConjecture.lean already formalizes. Reviewers may wish to check whether they want the n ≥ 3 variant included.
AMS tags `14 16` (algebraic geometry, associative rings and algebras): the Weyl algebra is MSC 16S32 and the problem's Wikipedia tag is algebraic geometry (via the Jacobian conjecture).

The Conjecture of Dixmier for the first Weyl algebra is true

reviewer_notes: The list entry is terse; the implicit hypotheses (base field of characteristic zero, endomorphism = unital k-algebra homomorphism, automorphism = bijective) were confirmed against Belov-Kanel–Kontsevich (arXiv:math/0512171, definition of DC_n and A_{n,k}) and Zheglov (arXiv:2410.06959, End_K(A_1) = Aut_K(A_1)). All eight candidates compiled cleanly in the checkout (verified) and all state the same proposition; the Weyl-algebra constructions (RingQuot, TwoSidedIdeal.ringCon.Quotient, Ideal quotient via .asIdeal with IsTwoSided) are all semantically correct presentations. No candidate omitted a slot. c02's extra declarations were deliberately not shipped: the conjunction `dixmier_conjecture` is redundant with the two slots, and `variants.not_of_three_le` (research solved, sorry'd) is outside the decomposition table and depends on the recent 3-variable Jacobian counterexample. Bespoke definitions are kept in the problem file as the task asked for a single file; a maintainer may prefer moving `WeylAlgebra` to FormalConjecturesForMathlib. Zero-based `Fin n` indexing is a relabeling only; the sign convention [∂,x]=1 vs Dixmier's [p,q]=1 gives the same algebra. Lines over 100 chars are only reference URLs in the module docstring, as elsewhere in the repository.
